chapter: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
title: The bus Paul Barbarin and Danny bought for the Louisiana tour
summary: After This Little Girl from Jacksonville became a hit in Louisiana and Texas, Paul told them to come south, and they bought and repaired a $400 bus that ran out of gas.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Finish talking, Lu, while I get tuned up here. Me and Terry (?), we came...in '54 we came to New Orleans -- about '54. It was '48 when we came down here, you know... No, we were in California. And Danny had written a tune called "This Little Girl From Jacksonville." So the tune was a hit in Louisiana and Texas. So Paul wrote us, and said, "Why don't you all come down here, because the tune is a hit." So we could tour Louisiana and Texas...

Paul Barbarin. So then we left California and we came here for a while. Paul had a little station wagon. He had a station wagon, but it was too small. So they went across the river and they seen a bus. So they came back, and they told me, Paul said, "We saw a bus, a good bus." "Why don't you all buy that bus? How much is this bus?" Paul said, "Four hundred dollars and we can get this bus." So I said, "All right." So I gave them the four hundred dollars, and they went to get the bus. When they got the bus... My mother was living down on the next block... They got the bus to the house, and then the bus wouldn't run! So they pushed the bus to the garage on Paris Avenue two blocks away. And when we got through fixing that bus and painting it up, it cost nine hundred dollars! But we used to go on
We would go with this bus. And Danny never did learn how to drive the bus, so we had pay somebody ten dollars every time we'd go out to drive the bus. And we took that bus up to New York...
With full brand-new tires. Remember them heavy-duty tires?

And we got three hundred dollars for it when we sold it. But it served the purpose, because it took us, you know, a lot of places. And each time, the first thing you know, the bus would stop, and I'd say, "What happened?" "No gas." Because the what'cha call it didn't...

Yeah, it didn't work. And oh, I'd get so mad. I'd say, "Didn't I tell you'all to get some gas?!" You know, we'd always be talking about the bus done stopped on the road. It was something riding that bus.
